ENG_001.context: In the as-built drawing, the wall axis differs from the latest revision of the working drawing.
ENG_001.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will compare the source measurements and the revisions to find the source of the discrepancy.
options.B: I will suspend the release and file a remark through the approval route.
options.C: I will check the measurements against the revision and register the discrepancy for approval.
options.D: I will ask the lead engineer for the grounds for the chosen revision and record the confirmed position of the wall.

ENG_002.context: A subcontractor has submitted quantities for completed work that exceed those recorded in the works log.
ENG_002.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will point out the specific discrepancy to the contractor and request a correction.
options.B: I will check the measurements against the log and propose correcting the quantities, giving my reasons.
options.C: I will compare the disputed items with the primary records and propose a reconciliation procedure to the contractor myself.
options.D: I will check the links to the work sections and the original measurements.

ENG_003.context: The handover package is missing the concealed work certificate for one joint.
ENG_003.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the primary records and, together with the site, restore a valid package.
options.B: I will collect the available confirmations from the site and check which stages can actually be traced.
options.C: I will pull up the log and the photo records and check the actual sequence.
options.D: I will contact the site and collect confirmed information from the people who did the work.

ENG_004.context: The site manager asks you to urgently send the client a statement with an unconfirmed date.
ENG_004.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will clarify the source of the date myself and record the confirmed value before sending the statement.
options.B: I will state directly that the date needs to be confirmed before sending.
options.C: I will record the request and submit the statement through the established approval process.
options.D: I will explain the risk and send the statement only after the date has been checked against documents.

ENG_005.context: At a meeting, two departments interpret the boundary of the contractor's scope differently.
ENG_005.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will present my verified interpretation based on the contract and drawings.
options.B: I will organise a short reconciliation with both departments and write down the questions.
options.C: I will show the calculation and help agree a common position with those responsible.
options.D: I will propose my interpretation of the boundaries and check it on the disputed items together with the departments.

ENG_006.context: Before the month-end submission, corrections to the as-built documentation register have piled up.
ENG_006.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will agree priorities with the site and help collect the missing attachments.
options.B: I will update the register, checking the sources, and share the collection of attachments with the site.
options.C: I will agree with colleagues on dividing up the corrections and establish the procedure for checking the updated register.
options.D: I will check each correction against the source document and update the statuses.

ENG_007.context: The incoming change record states the old concrete grade.
ENG_007.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the grade against the approved set and return the record formally.
options.B: I will compare the concrete grade with the current decision and register a clarification to the record.
options.C: I will check the chain of revisions and the source of the grade value.
options.D: I will register the error and send the document to be reissued.

ENG_008.context: The certificate of completed works lists a type of work that is not in the current estimate.
ENG_008.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the basis for the disputed quantity and personally propose a procedure for approving it separately.
options.B: I will compare the type of work with the contract and the basis for the change.
options.C: I will discuss with the person responsible the need for a proper basis before inclusion.
options.D: I will check the contract documents and make clear that the line needs to be justified.

ENG_009.context: At the client's request, a set of documents is needed for a joint completed several months ago.
ENG_009.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will trace the joint through the drawing, logs and certificates for the relevant period.
options.B: I will contact the archive and the site to quickly collect confirmations.
options.C: I will match the joint numbers with the logs and involve the archive in putting the package together.
options.D: I will ask the site to outline the stages of work on the joint and use them to check the contents of the archive set.

ENG_010.context: A colleague suggests signing the certificate while the as-built drawing has not yet been attached.
ENG_010.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the mandatory attachments and return the certificate according to the procedure.
options.B: I will explain the reason for the return and file a request for the missing drawing.
options.C: I will identify the missing attachments myself and set a deadline for checking the complete certificate package.
options.D: I will calmly point out that the package does not yet confirm the quantity.

ENG_011.context: The site is waiting for an answer on the status of a design change, but approval is delayed.
ENG_011.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the change register and communicate a single status to both teams.
options.B: I will propose to the site my own way of getting the status and agree feedback times with the participants.
options.C: I will report the verified status and clearly state which works are affected.
options.D: I will contact the design team and the site for a joint status update.

ENG_012.context: Several crews are submitting certificates at the same time with different designations for the same work section.
ENG_012.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will agree the section designations with the crews and record them in the rules for accepting certificates.
options.B: I will apply the agreed designation reference when checking each certificate.
options.C: I will gather the contractors and help them agree uniform designations.
options.D: I will check the certificates against the reference and send the participants the agreed template.

ENG_013.context: A discrepancy in units of measurement compared with the drawing was found in the materials list.
ENG_013.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will recalculate the item according to the specification and check the units.
options.B: I will stop the release of the list and file a request for correction.
options.C: I will check the units, recalculate the quantity and register the correction.
options.D: I will check the unit conversion on the disputed items and enter the confirmed values into the list.

ENG_014.context: During approval there is an argument about whether temporary fencing is a separate scope item.
ENG_014.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will formulate a position citing the contract clause and the source data.
options.B: I will check the grounds and present a reasoned calculation to the participants.
options.C: I will compare the fencing calculation with the contract terms and present the basis for my position myself.
options.D: I will study the contractual boundaries and the supporting statements.

ENG_015.context: For a recurring defect, it is hard to trace the room numbers in the defect reports.
ENG_015.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the causes of the errors and agree a single card template with the site.
options.B: I will collect examples of incomplete remarks together with the supervisors and find out at what stage the room number gets lost.
options.C: I will find the pattern of errors in the original remark records.
options.D: I will help the site introduce a clear template for designating rooms.

ENG_016.context: The contractor asks to enter an inspection date in the log that has not yet been confirmed.
ENG_016.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will request confirmation of the actual inspection myself and record a traceable date in the log.
options.B: I will refuse to enter an unconfirmed date and explain why.
options.C: I will make the entry only after checking the supporting materials according to the procedure.
options.D: I will explain the requirement and record the verified date after receiving the grounds.

ENG_017.context: A new supervisor does not understand which documents are needed before concreting.
ENG_017.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will list the required documents and explain the order of checking.
options.B: I will go through the package with him and help find the missing documents.
options.C: I will explain the requirements and check a specific package together with the supervisor.
options.D: I will suggest reviewing the package with the supervisor and take responsibility for explaining the disputed requirements.

ENG_018.context: Before the stage handover, several certificates are stuck with different approvers.
ENG_018.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will contact the approvers, find out what is blocking them and help collect what is missing.
options.B: I will update the register and help to remove the specific causes of delay.
options.C: I will agree the order of review with the approvers and update the dates in the certificate register.
options.D: I will check the register, the deadlines and the completeness of each certificate.

ENG_019.context: Two versions of an as-built drawing with the same date were found in the archive.
ENG_019.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the transmittal history and file a request about the current version.
options.B: I will compare the history of the two files with the change log and register the confirmed version.
options.C: I will compare the signatures, revision numbers and transmittal register.
options.D: I will mark both versions as disputed and request official confirmation.

ENG_020.context: When reconciling the schedule and the certificates, it turned out that a stage was closed in a different sequence.
ENG_020.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will compare the actual order with the acceptance conditions and personally propose a way of clarifying the certificates.
options.B: I will check the dates in the logs, the schedule and the certificates to establish the cause.
options.C: I will inform those responsible of the specific inconsistency and propose a reconciliation.
options.D: I will put together a confirmed chronology and confidently propose a correction.

ENG_021.context: The client keeps raising the same remarks about how the drawings are formatted.
ENG_021.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will classify the remarks and find the source of the repetition.
options.B: I will discuss a short memo with the drafters and help them apply it.
options.C: I will analyse the causes and update the drawing template together with the team.
options.D: I will collect examples of repeated issues together with the drawing authors and determine where the necessary information is lost.

ENG_022.context: To send the package, you are being required to sign on behalf of an absent approver.
ENG_022.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will find the substitution procedure provided for by the regulations.
options.B: I will point out the restriction and arrange approval through the appointed deputy.
options.C: I will personally arrange a request for an authorised substitute and follow the established signing procedure.
options.D: I will explain that only an authorised person can sign.

ENG_023.context: The site is sure the change has already been approved, but in the register it is listed as a draft.
ENG_023.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will show the register entry and arrange a quick confirmation from the author.
options.B: I will propose that the site check the status at a joint meeting and take on presenting the confirmed information.
options.C: I will clearly state the confirmed status and the consequences for the package.
options.D: I will connect the site with the author of the change and put together a single explanation.

ENG_024.context: At shift handover, some of the remarks on the as-built documentation remain open.
ENG_024.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will agree the list of open remarks with the new shift and assign who is responsible for following up.
options.B: I will set up a register with an owner, a deadline and a supporting document.
options.C: I will do a short handover and help colleagues understand the priorities.
options.D: I will update the register and personally go through the open items with the new shift.

ENG_025.context: In the federated BIM model, a new air duct intersects a load-bearing beam.
ENG_025.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the coordinates, levels and source requirements of both disciplines.
options.B: I will register the clash and assign it to those responsible according to the procedure.
options.C: I will check the geometry against the source data and create a task for coordination.
options.D: I will request the source constraints from the authors of the sections and register a confirmed clash task.

ENG_026.context: The architectural and structural models contain different finished floor levels.
ENG_026.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will present the specific discrepancy to the team and propose establishing a single datum.
options.B: I will check the sources of the levels and propose a single datum, giving my reasons.
options.C: I will compare the basis of both floor levels and propose a question for a joint decision myself.
options.D: I will compare the revisions and the datum levels in the design briefs.

ENG_027.context: The same clash with utility networks occurs regularly in standard details.
ENG_027.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will identify the cause and help the team update the standard detail.
options.B: I will collect recurring cases together with the authors of the details and check which dependency causes the clash.
options.C: I will determine which placement rule creates the repetition.
options.D: I will discuss with the modellers a common way of preventing such clashes.

ENG_028.context: The site is requesting a drawing, although the latest version is still under review.
ENG_028.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will personally arrange clarification of the drawing status and establish the procedure for issuing the confirmed version.
options.B: I will clearly report the status and indicate the approved version to be used.
options.C: I will check the release route and the availability of the current set.
options.D: I will explain the status and pass on a link only to the approved release.

ENG_029.context: The contractor proposes shifting the cable route to avoid an intersection.
ENG_029.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will set out the technical constraints and say that the decision requires review.
options.B: I will gather the designers of the adjacent systems for a joint review.
options.C: I will state the constraints and arrange approval of an alternative route.
options.D: I will propose my own way of presenting the change and refine it with the contractor for the model authors.

ENG_030.context: In the model, several people have created different names for identical families.
ENG_030.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will help the team bring the families in line with a common reference.
options.B: I will update the list according to the standard and carry out a joint check with the authors.
options.C: I will agree a single naming principle with the authors and build it into the check of new families.
options.D: I will check the names against the BIM standard and draw up a list of corrections.
